scores.counterexample: For a source i and successor j, log_{x_j}(x_i) points from x_j toward x_i. Parallel-transporting it to x_i still points toward the source; negating it is required to represent the source-to-successor direction. Omitting that negation flips every vector, while pairwise cosines remain unchanged if all vectors are flipped together—so the loss cannot identify this global sign.

scores.counterexample: For a single-successor source i with successor j, μ_i=x_j. Therefore PT_{x_i→0}(log_{x_i}(μ_i)) equals the behavior-weighted mean of PT_{x_i→0}(log_{x_i}(x_j)); their difference is exactly 0, and the stated loss has zero gradient for that source.

Under a consistent tangent-space mean and transport convention, those are the same quantity, making the Huber loss identically zero rather than a training signal.
